detail.Title: Senior Manager, Data Strategy & Analytics - GO-SEMI
detail.Duties Description: *Applicants MUST submit a cover letter with resume to be considered. *This position will require in-office presence. Hybrid work schedules may be possible based on specific job duties and consistent with ESD policy. *Minorities, women, and individuals with disabilities are encouraged to apply. Please contact Human Resources if you require accommodation. BASIC FUNCTION: The Senior Manager, Data Strategy and Analytics leads GO-SEMI’s data strategy and translates complex information into practical guidance for New York’s semiconductor expansion. Reporting directly to the Director of Strategy & Operations, the Manager establishes reliable data across GO-SEMI programs and develops analysis that helps leadership prioritize investments, identify delivery risks, and assess results. The role combines hands-on business intelligence and CRM expertise with sound analytical judgment and the ability to explain findings to non-technical audiences. This is an opportunity to build data and analytics capability supporting New York’s long-term semiconductor growth. The Manager will shape GO-SEMI’s analytics roadmap and work closely with program leaders, ESD Information Technology (IT), GIS specialists, and external partners. The portfolio spans workforce development, site readiness and infrastructure, business recruitment, supply chain expansion, supplier readiness, Green CHIPS, SGAP, and emerging initiatives. Microsoft Dynamics 365 and Microsoft Power BI are core tools; the role also connects information across programs to show where needs are growing, where delivery is falling behind, and which interventions warrant attention. WORK PERFORMED: Data Strategy and Cross Program Analysis • Analytics Roadmap: Develop and maintain a prioritized data and reporting roadmap with leadership. Translate program needs into defined deliverables, sequence foundational data work before advanced analytics, and recommend the staffing, vendor support, and tools needed to maintain the capability as GO-SEMI grows. • Cross-Program Analysis: Link company and project records across recruitment, supplier readiness, sites, and workforce programs. Work with program leads to identify overlapping demand, service gaps, and dependencies that individual program reports may miss. • Partner and Portal Integration: Define data requirements and acceptance criteria for the Connectivity Portal and other partner systems. Coordinate with IT and vendors on integration, data-sharing arrangements, common identifiers, and validation so external information can be used reliably in internal reporting. Executive Reporting and Program Performance • Decision-Focused Reporting: Build Power BI dashboards and concise executive analyses that connect recruitment pipelines, project milestones, site readiness, supplier participation, workforce needs, and program expenditures. Highlight the decision or follow-up each finding calls for, with intuitive drill-down views for program staff. • Performance Measures: Agree on KPI definitions, baselines, targets, and reporting frequency with program owners. Distinguish announced commitments, contracted obligations, disbursements, and verified outcomes; document methods to prevent double counting across companies, projects, and programs. • Self-Service Reporting: Create accessible reporting templates and guidance that enable staff to answer routine questions independently. Use appropriate access controls and separate reporting from source-data editing, in coordination with IT. Trend Analysis and Scenario Planning • Historical Reporting: Establish reliable monthly, quarterly, and annual snapshots and change histories with IT and platform specialists. Preserve the ability to compare results over time and reproduce previously reported figures as project schedules and records change. • Data Modeling: Develop relational and Power BI data models, including DAX measures, that support consistent program totals, historical comparisons, and analysis across GO-SEMI workstreams. Document source systems, refresh schedules, and limitations. • Forecasting and Early Warning: Analyze how changes in fab schedules and supplier activity affect workforce demand, site and utility readiness, and program delivery. Develop scenarios with program experts, state assumptions and uncertainty, and distinguish forecasts from verified results. Flag bottlenecks and emerging gaps for leadership action. CRM Product Ownership and IT Partnership • GO-SEMI Platform Leadership: Serve as the business owner and technical lead for GO-SEMI’s CRM and analytics requirements. Maintain a prioritized enhancement backlog and coordinate delivery with ESD IT, Dynamics 365 specialists, and consultants. IT retains responsibility for enterprise infrastructure, cybersecurity, and production change approvals. • CRM Configuration and Integration: Configure and improve GO-SEMI workflows, fields, reporting, and data validation within approved access and change-management procedures. Define requirements for complex integrations and schema changes and coordinate specialist implementation and testing. • Green CHIPS Reporting: Develop the data structure, collection workflows, and reporting tools for annual Green CHIPS reporting in partnership with program, finance, and legal staff. Maintain supporting evidence and audit trails; program owners remain responsible for validating submissions and determining compliance. • Data Stewardship and Reporting Controls: Coordinate with IT and legal staff on permissions, retention, secure sharing, and approval of external reporting. Define refresh schedules and escalation procedures for failed updates or unresolved discrepancies; show the date and reliability of information used in leadership reports. • Data Quality and Governance: Establish a common data dictionary, unique identifiers, source-of-record rules, and quality checks across company, site, project, supplier, and participant records. Assign data owners and update expectations with program leads, track missing or stale information, and reconcile discrepancies before executive or external reporting. Geospatial Analysis and Site Readiness • Spatial Analysis: Work with GO-SEMI’s GIS staff and program experts to analyze site readiness, supplier locations, workforce access, and relevant infrastructure constraints. Connect geographic information to technical site requirements and readiness scorecards so leadership can compare options and identify investment gaps. • GIS Integration: Connect authoritative GIS datasets with CRM records and Power BI reporting in partnership with GIS specialists and IT. Maintain consistent site identifiers, source dates, and geographic definitions, with appropriate controls for sensitive company and parcel information. Implementation and User Adoption • Testing and Release: Lead business user acceptance testing for new workflows, dashboards, and integrations. Agree on acceptance criteria with program owners and IT, test data accuracy and permissions, and document issues before release. • Process Improvement and Automation: Simplify data collection and recurring reporting through reusable workflows and automation. Evaluate emerging tools, including AI-assisted analysis, through approved ESD processes, with human review of outputs and safeguards for confidential information. • Training and Documentation: Train staff and partners on data entry, interpretation, and reporting. Maintain practical documentation and measure adoption through usage, reporting turnaround time, and data quality. Design repeatable processes that can be supported by others. Additional Operational Support • Ad-Hoc Projects & Other Duties: Perform other related technical, analytical, or data-driven duties as assigned by leadership to support the evolving needs of the GO-SEMI initiative and Empire State Development priorities.
detail.Minimum Qualifications: Education Level Required: Bachelor’s degree in data analytics, information systems, computer science, statistics, GIS, economics, public policy, or a related field. Consider an equivalent combination of relevant education and demonstrated professional experience, subject to ESD hiring requirements. Experience Required: 5+ years of progressively responsible experience in business intelligence, data analytics, CRM implementation, or related work, including leading a significant reporting or systems initiative. Demonstrated ability to build useful dashboards, improve data quality, and translate analysis into recommendations for non-technical decision-makers. Knowledge Required: • CRM and Data Management: Hands-on experience configuring, supporting, or implementing an enterprise CRM and connecting it to reporting workflows. Ability to define data requirements and work effectively with IT and vendors. Dynamics 365 experience is preferred; candidates with comparable platform experience should demonstrate the ability to become proficient in ESD’s environment. • Business Intelligence and Analysis: Strong Power BI skills, including data modeling, DAX, drill-through reporting, and appropriate access controls. Proficiency in SQL and relational data concepts; experience documenting analytical methods, testing data quality, and presenting findings and limitations clearly. • Leadership and Collaboration: Ability to manage competing priorities, lead delivery across program and technical teams, train users, and communicate concise recommendations to senior leadership. Sound judgment in handling confidential company and participant information. Preferred Experience: Dynamics 365 or Dataverse; ArcGIS Pro or ArcGIS Online; APIs and data integration; Python or R; and scenario analysis. Experience in economic development, capital projects, workforce programs, or semiconductor-related industries is valuable. The role should be supported by GIS and enterprise IT specialists for advanced platform work.

detail.Duties Description: OPWDD's Division of State Operations (DSO) is responsible for overseeing the delivery of state operated supports and services to over 8,000 recipients across New York State. This Data Analyst 1 position sits within DSO's Bureau of Business Analytics and Research, which is responsible for overseeing all Division activities involving operational research, program evaluation, data reporting, and analytics. This includes the development and maintenance of in-house applications and coordination with vendors regarding external software solutions. The Bureau of Business Analytics and Research as currently structured is organized into three business level units: (1) Enterprise Software Solutions, (2) Application Development, and (3) Data, Statistics and Operational Research. The selected candidate will join the Application Development Unit. This unit is responsible for the design, development, and maintenance of SharePoint solutions. detail.Title: Food Web Analysis Using Stable Isotopes Intern
detail.Duties Description: The NY DEC DLF BISEH’s Invasive Species Coordination Section is seeking an intern to assist with a study that will use previously collected tissue sample from plants and animals to describe the food web along the upper Hudson River prior to the introduction of round goby. The intern will be responsible for homogenizing tissues using mortar and pestle (and other methods), weighing out and packaging the samples using a microbalance. When results are received from the analysis lab, the intern will assist with data analysis. Use of Microsoft Office, and Program R will be incorporated into the project. The intern will assist with new sample collection as it occurs. Daily tasks include manual homogenization of tissue samples, weighing/packaging samples for analysis, data entry, data manipulation and analysis.

detail.Duties Description: The New York State Digital Service team at the Office of General Services (OGS) seeks an experienced digital strategy professional to serve as the Content Strategy Manager. detail.Duties Description: Executive Division Research and Analytics Department—NYC Data Scientist Reference No. RAD_NYC_DAS_6463 Application Deadline is November 13, 2026 Salary is $116,233 + $4,150 in location pay To be considered for this opportunity, submit a complete application online at https://ag.ny.gov/job-postings/other Goal: The Research and Analytics Department in the Office of the New York State Attorney General (OAG) is seeking candidates for a full-time Data Scientist position. Data Scientists at OAG bring their skills to bear across a wide variety of cases and investigations. The Data Scientist will utilize a vast array of tools to explore datasets, develop new databases, and use statistical modeling to detect anomalies in information pertinent to OAG investigations. The goal of the Data Scientist at OAG is to ensure that our most complicated cases and policy arenas have the benefit of advanced analytical tools, methodologies, and strategic thinking to understand how otherwise elusive trends can be laid bare once we dive into the underlying data. Purview: As part of an innovative team housed in the Executive Division, you will work with senior staff and divisions throughout OAG to support OAG's major initiatives, investigations, and policy development. Our team researches and writes analytical reports garnering national attention, directs multi-million-dollar grant programs, and supports OAG’s major investigations. See for example: lawsuit against auto lender for deceptive practices, preliminary report on NYPD response to Protests, JUUL lawsuit and remediation, opioids lawsuit, lawsuit preserving affordable housing from illegal kickback scheme, and the FCC fake comments report. Utilizing a vast collection of public and confidential information, you will work with data covering the breadth of OAG’s purview building advanced analytic tools to inform investigations that affect the lives of all New Yorkers. Employing over 2,000 people across New York state, OAG is both the “People's Lawyer” and the state's chief legal officer. The Data Scientist will support OAG work in numerous legal and regulatory arenas, including protecting the rights of investors and consumers, coordinating state-wide criminal investigations, promoting civil rights, economic and social justice, encouraging harm-reducing public health strategies, and preserving the state’s environment. The OAG also advises the Executive branch of state government and defends actions and proceedings on behalf of the state. Duties: Data can and does play a pivotal role in decisioning on a wide range of OAG’s work. The Data Scientist will be primarily responsible for: • All aspects of using data to develop and test legal hypotheses, including: o Brainstorming with legal teams on the data required o Acquiring data through public sources and assisting legal teams to acquire data from confidential sources to ensure the delivery of data sufficient for investigation o Testing data for reliability o Distilling and incorporating relevant academic and other analytical research o Developing and executing appropriate methodologies for data exploration and analysis o Clearly communicating findings verbally and through written reports and visualizations, including relevant limitations o Continuously updating analysis in the face of feedback and new data o Quantifying uncertainty in analytical findings • Working closely with legal teams on all the aspects above and providing guidance and recommendations on decision making around data • Additional responsibilities may include: o Developing predictive modeling to detect anomalies o Developing or programming new databases or data tools o Writing fact and expert reports for submission to the court and defending analysis and findings in depositions o Helping to maintain and improve the team’s shared computational infrastructure o Staying informed of the latest advances in data tools and techniques and sharing newfound skills with the team o Performing other duties as requested

detail.Duties Description: The State University of New York, or SUNY, is the largest comprehensive system of public higher education in the United States, with 64 colleges and universities spanning the state from Long Island to the Adirondacks to Buffalo. SUNY System Administration employees, based in Albany and New York City, provide critical support for SUNY campuses, employees, and students to advance SUNY's mission of providing high-quality, affordable higher education for all. Across a wide range of roles, from finance and legal counsel to student support, academic affairs, IT, admissions, and more, our employees work toward advancing the four priority pillars established by SUNY Chancellor John B. King Jr. and the SUNY Board of Trustees: student success; research and scholarship; diversity, equity, and inclusion; and economic development and upward mobility. SUNY System Administration is a mission-driven workplace with robust New York State benefits including health insurance, retirement, time off, and paid family leave. The Director of SUNY Information Technology Optimization and Engagement provides leadership for projects and portfolio management across the SUNY Office of Information Technology under the direction of the Chief Information Officer (CIO). The Director leads and supports a project management office responsible for establishing consistent project management policies and practices, coordinating work across the OIT portfolio, and providing leadership with clear information about project status, costs, schedules, risks, dependencies, resource needs, and expected outcomes. The Director is responsible for ensuring IT projects are aligned with SUNY's strategic goals and portfolio management priorities driving alignment and engagement across 64 campuses and SUNY hospitals for campus and central administration technology operations. detail.Duties Description: The New York State Education Department's (NYSED) Office of Information Technology Services (ITS) is seeking applicants for multiple Information Technology Specialist 2 positions. These positions offer opportunities in many different areas, including, but not limited to: • Web application development leveraging technologies such as Java, JavaScript, and SQL; • Server and networking support for our in-house data center as well as Cloud infrastructure; • Database Administration for Oracle, SQL Server, and MySQL databases; • Application Integration support for API Services, Continuous Delivery; • Low-code platform development and administration; • UX Design and Development; and • Enterprise Help Desk Support and Automation. The NYSED is committed to implementing progressive technologies. The positions available require a willingness and aptitude to learn quickly. detail.Title: Information Technology Specialist 2 (Programming) (NY HELPS), Box Info Tech Spec 2 (Prog)
detail.Street Address: Office of Performance Improvement and Management Services
detail.Duties Description: The New York State Education Department’s (NYSED) Office of Performance Improvement and Management Services is seeking candidates for multiple Information Technology Specialist 2 (Programming) positions in the Office of Information Technology Services. The incumbents of these positions will serve as members of the Business Solutions team, providing programming support for NYSED's enterprise applications, and developing Information Technology (IT) solutions to support the business needs of NYSED. Duties of this position include, but are not limited to, the following: • Develop and maintain IT solutions and web applications written in Java, SQL, Javascript/VueJS, PL/SQL, HTML, and CSS/SASS. This includes new analysis and development, troubleshooting, testing, and deployment; • Collaborate with program office and IT staff to understand, document, and implement business requirements; • Design, maintain, and modify Oracle SQL databases to support web applications; • Ensure all code has unit and integration testing in place prior to deployment; • Identify and troubleshoot problems and subsequently offer and implement necessary solutions; • Take part in a traineeship to determine programming skill levels while offering the opportunity to improve proficiency in multiple disciplines; • Utilize department standards for work tracking and version control, including the use of Jira, Confluence, and Git; • Ensure that systems and procedures are properly documented, meet Department standards, and follow generally accepted IT practices, so as to foster the integrity of data and automated systems; The following skills and abilities are essential to successful performance of the job: • Knowledge and practical experience programming in Java, SQL and/or VueJS. • Knowledge and experience with the design, implementation, and usage of a database. • Knowledge and experience with a Model-View-Controller (MVC) web application and/or service-oriented architecture.
